Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

1,530 of 1,825 sentences in this record
Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
PMET workforce and EA coverage

54% of resident workforce are PMETs and 34% PMEs, and PMEs earning over $4,500 monthly are not covered under the Employment Act.

  2. s00003 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    Today, 54% of our resident workforce are professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) and 34% are professionals, managers and executives (PMEs).

  3. s00004 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coastcontext

    There have been many PMEs approaching the Labour Movement for help via our various workplace advisory platforms with a variety of issues from unfair dismissals to breaches of provisions in the Employment Act (EA).

  4. s00005 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

    However, PMEs with a monthly basic salary of more than $4,500 are not covered under the Act.

    • Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
    Three proposed EA changes

    Proposes expanding EA scope to cover PMEs beyond $4,500, extending Part IV protection beyond $2,500, and enhancing dispute resolution.

    1. s00012 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

      First, expansion of the scope of EA to cover PMEs beyond the current $4,500 limit; second, extension of the Part IV protection to cover non-workmen beyond the current $2,500 limit; and third, enhancements to the existing dispute resolution framework.

    • Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
    Removing $4,500 salary cap

    Questions the PME versus Rank and File dichotomy and proposes removing the $4,500 salary cap so all employees get EA protection.

    1. s00017 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coastcontext

      In fact, whether there is a need to have this "PME versus Rank and File" dichotomy is something we need to review whether now or in the near future.

    2. s00018 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

      I submit, therefore, we should remove this $4,500 salary cap completely so that all employees in Singapore can enjoy the basic protection under EA.

    • Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
    Reviewing salary limits

    Submits that the $2,500 and $4,500 limits need review and raising to keep pace with rising median wages.

    1. s00021 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

      To keep pace with wage movements, I submit there is a need to review both the $2,500 and $4,500 limits accordingly and raise it to keep pace with rising median wages.

    • Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
    Section 18A employee transfers

    Section 18A allows for the transfer of employees to a new entity.

    1. s00031 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

      Section 18A allows for the transfer of employees to a new entity.

    • Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan · Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
    Three EA review areas

    Lists removing the salary ceiling, raising the Part 4 non-manual workers cap, and enhancing dispute mediation, noting PMEs earning $4,500 or more lack EA protection.

    1. s00041 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

      First of all, we should remove the salary ceiling to cover all workers, including PMEs with monthly salary exceeding $4,500, so that they will all be protected under EA.

    2. s00042 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

      Second, with the rise in median salary, the monthly salary cap of non-manual workers covered under Part 4 of the EA should also increase.

    3. s00043 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

      Third, the current dispute mediation framework should also be enhanced, for example, to allow the ECT to handle unfair dismissal cases.

    4. s00044 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coastcontext

      (In English): In summary, these three areas are important areas for review to ensure the EA stays relevant and serves the needs of the future workforce, the future of work and the future of workplaces.

    5. s00045 · 840Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan — West Coast

      However, we must bear in mind that the amendments should not compromise the need to preserve effective collective bargaining and bring more workers within the tripartite relationship.

    7. s00047 · 840Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      Mr Chairman, currently, PMEs who earn a basic salary of $4,500 or more are not protected under the EA.

    8. s00048 · 840Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar — Ang Mo Kio

      According to recent employment data, the median gross salary of resident employees is about $4,050 a month.
